title: 'Loud Working' Is the New Workplace Trend
paragraphs: Do you have a colleague who is always talking about their latest success? They may be part of a new workplace trend called "loud working."

Loud working means making your work very visible to others. This can include posting about your successes on social media sites like LinkedIn, sharing updates on work chat apps such as Slack or Teams, and speaking up a lot in meetings.

According to research by Tide, a financial services company, the average worker in the UK spends about 2.8 hours a week making their work visible. That adds up to 131 hours a year, or about 17 working days. Young workers seem to do it the most. Nearly 70% of people aged 25 to 34 say they are loud working, and they spend about five hours a week promoting themselves.

For many people, loud working seems to pay off. According to the research, 77% of loud workers had at least one career opportunity in the past year, such as a pay rise, a promotion or new clients. In addition, 17% said they got a new job because they talked more about their work.

However, not everyone likes this trend. About 27% of workers said they had thought about leaving a job because of loud working culture or colleagues who talk too much about themselves. One in ten said they had actually left a job because of it.
Some experts believe the trend is connected to fears about job security. When people are worried about losing their jobs, they may feel they need to show their bosses how hard they are working.

George Schmidt, an executive at Tide, said there is a difference between being performative and believing in yourself. In other words, it is good to share your success, but it should not become more important than the work itself.
